iti110:1.1: This was said by the Blessed One, said by the Arahant, so I have heard:
iti110:2.1: “If, while he is walking, monks, there arises in a monk a thought of sensuality, a thought of ill-will, or a thought of harmfulness,
iti110:2.2: and he does not quickly abandon, dispel, demolish, or wipe that thought out of existence, then a monk walking with such a lack of ardency & compunction is called continually & continuously lethargic & low in his persistence.
iti110:3.1: “If, while he is standing.… “If, while he is sitting.… “If, while he is lying down, there arises in a monk a thought of sensuality, a thought of ill-will, or a thought of harmfulness,
iti110:5.2: and he does not quickly abandon, dispel, demolish, or wipe that thought out of existence,
iti110:5.3: then a monk lying down with such a lack of ardency & compunction is called continually & continuously lethargic & low in his persistence.
iti110:6.1: “But if, while he is walking, there arises in a monk a thought of sensuality, a thought of ill-will, or a thought of harmfulness,
iti110:6.2: and he quickly abandons, dispels, demolishes, & wipes that thought out of existence,
iti110:6.3: then a monk walking with such ardency & compunction is called continually & continuously resolute, one with persistence aroused.
iti110:7.1: “If, while he is standing.… “If, while he is sitting.… “If, while he is lying down, there arises in a monk a thought of sensuality, a thought of ill-will, or a thought of harmfulness,
iti110:9.2: and he quickly abandons, dispels, demolishes, & wipes that thought out of existence,
iti110:9.3: then a monk lying down with such ardency & compunction is called continually & continuously resolute, one with persistence aroused.”
